items.title: Edmond Hall Interview, 1957-04-11
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Did you know Blind Mac, by any chance... I doubt if you would... [INTERVIEWEE] Well, different bands, I worked with quite a few different bands.

ctx.x: It'd be nice to find out. I don't know.

I don't know. I don't know. Did you know Blind Mac, by any chance, he played piano and sang around Jacksonville? I doubt if you would, he just played blues, played pretty nice. I don't know. I guess all the things on Lonnie Johnson's own style singing. Some of the people are, you know, I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. I don't know. Some of the people that you worked with in New York, got a player, different bands.

Well, different bands, I worked with quite a few different bands. I worked with, let's see, can I get them in rotation? When you first got there, I was thinking about you. When I first got there, well, I went there with Ross's band. We only stayed on the job about two weeks. Then I went into a dancing school with another, by the way it was a piano player down in Florida that was in New York. He went to New York with this Broadway gentleman. So when we got to New York and working at a big place like the Roseland,…
